title: Show what the button promises before building it
question: How can we tell whether an AI-designed button will actually do what its explanation promises?
answer: ASE is a place for human-guided AI software development through voluntary contribution and shared learning. The supplied October 19 research digest describes “Design Theater” (F21), a 2026 study of the gap between generative UI tools’ design reasoning and their implementation; the digest rates this MEDIUM confidence, and we have not independently verified the paper. We propose showing a synthetic, non-executing walkthrough beside each proposed UI change’s acceptance wording: initial state, human action, visible consequence and failure response. To check whether this helps, compare prose-only review with walkthrough-assisted review across six synthetic proposals containing planted inconsistencies, including a silent failure and a misleading confirmation; the target is at least 80% detection, improvement over baseline and no reviewer mistaking the walkthrough for executed software. This would make ASE’s design promises easier to inspect before implementation, without replacing execution evidence or human acceptance.
